statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - Online Name Reservation System (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in French; a bilingual name is acceptable if French version is present and predominant. Latin-script romanization is required for non-French names. The name must comply with the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11) and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Suffix must be 'Inc.' or 'Corp.' and must be included. A clear distinctive component in French is generally required.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may request a formal administrative review by sending a written request to the Directeur de l'état civil / Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of the refusal notice. The request must include the rejected name, reasons submitted, and a proposed alternative. If the review confirms rejection, the applicant may appeal to the Court of Québec under s. 60 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises within 60 days. Name reservation extensions can be requested prior to expiry for one further period, generally 90 days, upon payment of the prescribed fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable under Quebec law provided a physical address in Quebec is registered and a registered agent is actively designated to receive legal service; the registered office cannot be a mere post-office box. Virtual office service providers with local presence and mail handling are permissible for this wholesale distribution industry subject to satisfactory client due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low likelihood due to non-high-risk wholesale activity (ISIC 4663). Estimated probability of unannounced on-site inspection in the first 12 months is below 5%; inspection may occur if AML/CFT indicators emerge or upon politically exposed person (PEP) related transactions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (Loi sur les sociétés par actions), CQLR c S-31.1, Part II (incorporation and share structure) and Part III (directors, registered office, officers); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 (registration with Registraire des entreprises); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11 (French corporate name requirement).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The QBCA does not impose any minimum paid-up capital. A share may be without par value; directors must fix the lawful consideration and must not issue a share until it is fully paid in cash, property or past services. No escrow account, capital deposit or bank confirmation is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Corporation subscribe to the shares set out in the articles of incorporation; that the directors allot and issue shares upon lawful consideration fixed by the board; and that issued shares be entered in the securities register. RESOLVED that the registered office be established at [address], Quebec, and that corporate records be maintained there. RESOLVED that [name] be appointed President, [name] Secretary, and [name] Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until successors are elected; and that each officer, acting alone, execute all instruments and filings to complete the incorporation and open banking accounts.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) for federal income tax and GST/HST, operating through the My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html); Revenu Québec for Quebec provincial income tax, QST (TVQ) and other provincial levies, operating through the CLIC portal (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/); Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for export declarations; Corporations Canada (federal) and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec for corporate registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned entity first incorporates as a business corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Quebec Business Corporations Act, obtaining a Quebec NEQ (Numero d'entreprise du Quebec) through the Registraire des entreprises. The corporation then obtains a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) via CRA's Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1, together with program accounts: RC for corporate income tax, RT for GST/HST, and RP for payroll. Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada or making taxable supplies in Canada must register for GST/HST even without a permanent establishment; voluntary registration is available to claim input tax credits. For QST, the corporation must file an initial registration with Revenu Quebec (via the one-stop registraire process) and obtain a separate QST (TVQ) account. The corporation must appoint a director resident in Canada (or a provincial nominee if Quebec-elected), maintain a registered office, and may be required to provide a Canadian resident agent for service. Forms and filings are administered jointly by CRA and Revenu Quebec, with the tax identity becoming effective upon issuance of the BN/NEQ.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box pass-through election; business corporations are per se taxable entities. Relevant elections and mechanisms include: GST/HST closely-related corporation election under ETA s. 156 (nil-consideration intra-group supplies); QST equivalent election for closely-related corporations under Quebec QST legislation; ITA s. 216(1) election for non-residents to compute Part I tax on net rental and royalty income instead of Part XIII withholding; ITA s. 219 branch profits tax election for Canadian branches of foreign corporations; ETA s. 179 election permitting non-resident registrants to claim an immediate refund of GST/HST; and hybrid mismatch compliance via ITA ss. 18.2-18.6 including the EIFEL limitation, which permits a group-level filing approach rather than elective entity reclassification. No retroactive entity-classification election is available, and treaty-based reductions require proving treaty entitlement and filing the appropriate waiver or reduced-withholding certificate.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-added tax comprising federal GST (Goods and Services Tax, 5%) administered by CRA and Quebec QST (Quebec Sales Tax / TVQ, 9.975%) administered by Revenu Quebec, giving a combined nominal VAT rate of 14.975% in Quebec; both are invoice-based credit-method VAT systems.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - small supplier threshold calculated on total worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies, but excluding financial services, supplies of goodwill and certain real property supplies) made in the four immediately preceding consecutive calendar quarters. A one-calendar-quarter exceedance of CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies also triggers mandatory registration effective the first day of the following month. For QST, the equivalent threshold is CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies made in Quebec over four consecutive quarters, with the same one-quarter exceedance rule. Export supplies, while zero-rated, are counted for threshold purposes, so an active bulk-cement exporter will likely exceed the threshold in its first fiscal quarter and must register from inception.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or pre-clearance API regime exists in Canada or Quebec as of 2025. Electronic invoicing is voluntary and follows the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Standard based on the Peppol BIS 3.0 network, with CRA and Revenu Quebec progressively participating and publishing transacting-party onboarding requirements. GST/HST and QST invoices must satisfy substantive content requirements under ETA s. 223 and the Quebec Tax Administration Act, including registrant name and BN/NEQ, invoice date, description of the supply, consideration, and either the applicable tax amount or a clear 'tax included' notation. For export shipments, the exporter must file the CBSA B13A export declaration electronically through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) or the legacy CAED system, citing the cargo control number of the ocean vessel, and retain the customs receipt number for audit trail purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Bulk hydraulic portland cement and clinker supplied for export are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V as supplies of tangible personal property exported by or on behalf of the supplier, provided that: (i) the goods are shipped from Canada by ocean vessel as soon after the supply as is reasonable, with CRA generally accepting a 60-day export window; (ii) title transfers to a non-resident recipient for use or consumption outside Canada; (iii) the goods are not substantially transformed or consumed in Canada prior to export; and (iv) the supplier obtains and retains contemporaneous documentary evidence of physical export, including the vessel departure date and foreign port of discharge. Ocean freight and related services supplied by the registrant for international carriage of those goods are separately zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part VII. QST zero-rating applies by reference to equivalent export rules under the Quebec QST Act for goods exported from Canada by the supplier. Where the goods are exported after more than 60 days or the documentary evidence is incomplete, the supply is taxable at 14.975% and the supplier must self-assess and remit the uncollected tax.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Form B13A Export Declaration filed via CERS/CAED with electronic cargo control number and customs receipt confirmation
Original or certified true copy of the ocean Bill of Lading showing the exporting shipper, outbound vessel call, port of loading in Canada, foreign port of discharge, and bulk commodity description
Commercial invoice and packing list referencing the exporter's Business Number (BN) and, where applicable, GST/HST and QST registration numbers
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 wire transfer confirmation from the foreign buyer evidencing receipt of export proceeds within the contractual payment term
Draft survey report, weight certificate, certificate of quality/quantity, and independent inspection certificate for the bulk clinker cargo
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Quebec may reassess within four years of the original assessment; the limitation period is unlimited where the taxpayer has made a misrepresentation, committed fraud, or wilfully defaulted. If export zero-rating is denied for deficient documentation or unreasonable export delay, the full GST/QST becomes payable, plus compound daily prescribed-rate interest from the date the tax was required to be collected. Civil penalties include the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the unremitted tax for knowingly making false statements or gross negligence under ETA s. 285 and the Quebec Tax Administration Act, and a 50% gross-negligence penalty on the understated income tax under ITA s. 163(2). Criminal conviction for tax evasion under ETA s. 327 or ITA s. 239 carries fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years. Canada imposes no statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline; however, CRA may scrutinize open export receivables exceeding normal commercial terms as a transfer-pricing indicator under ITA s. 247, and a non-arm's-length receivable outstanding beyond the reassessment window may trigger both provincial and federal currency-translation adjustments and penalty exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under QBCA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing administrative penalty of CAD 100–1,000; failure to file for 3 consecutive fiscal years permits the Registraire to dissolve the corporation by administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month late (maximum 12 months), with a minimum penalty of CAD 100; interest compounds daily on any outstanding balance; repeated non-filing may lead to criminal prosecution and revocation of tax clearance certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the tax due plus 1% per full month late (maximum 12 months); daily compounding interest; administrative fines and potential criminal prosecution for wilful evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Filing of Annual Meeting Resolutions and Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporation's own head office (minute book); no government filing unless changes require REQ update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held within 15 months after the preceding AGM and no later than 6 months after fiscal year-end (as determined by the articles/bylaws); in any event, no more than 18 months after incorporation for the first AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be subject to summary prosecution in Quebec for failure to call the AGM; shareholders may apply to the Superior Court for an order compelling the meeting or, after persistent default, for liquidation or dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registers and Ultimate Beneficiary Confirmation Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (for registry changes); maintained at registered office (for the statutory registers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation during the year; any change in directors, officers, registered office, or ultimate beneficiary status must be filed within 15 days of the change; annual confirmation is embedded in the Annual Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update the UBO register or transfer register can render share transfers unperfected; the Registraire may assess administrative penalties up to CAD 500 per failure and may refuse subsequent filings; continued non-compliance may trigger registry cancellation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is required for a Quebec business corporation that is a reporting issuer (publicly traded), has more than 20 shareholders, or where shareholders holding at least 10% of the voting shares demand an audit. A private, closely held corporation may avoid the appointment of an auditor by unanimous shareholder resolution adopted at each annual meeting.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public enterprises must file in accordance with IFRS; private enterprises may elect Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) as set out in the CPA Canada Handbook, with reconciling disclosures where applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec law requires every business corporation to maintain an ultimate beneficiary register identifying any individual who directly or indirectly holds 25% or more of voting rights or a significant control-in-fact over the corporation. The register must be updated within 30 days of any change; the annual declaration to the Registraire requires confirmation that the UBO register is complete and current as of the filing date. For share transfers, the register of members must record each transfer with the date, consideration, and new member details before the Annual Declaration is accepted.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 200–600 (USD 146–438) per year depending on service provider location in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 7,500–25,000 (USD 5,475–18,250) for a wholesale construction-materials distributor with annual revenue in the CAD 1–10 million range

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPC) reduces combined rate to 14% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income; additional investment tax credits for manufacturing and processing activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically via CRA NETFILE or approved tax preparation software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end due June 30).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue (gross sales and other income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Canadian-source income only; allocate revenue based on permanent establishment.
Apply Part I tax rate; consider treaty non-resident exemptions.
Compute at 15% federal rate; claim treaty credits if applicable.
File separate Quebec TP-1 return; apply Quebec tax credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of balance due plus 1% per month up to 12 months; interest on unpaid amounts at prescribed rates; additional penalties for repeated failures.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Part XIII tax on dividends paid to non-residents)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced treaty rate, non-resident must provide a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) and submit Form NR301 (or NR302 for corporations) to the Canadian payer; payer must withhold at treaty rate if conditions met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: royalties 25%, interest 25%. Under Canada-US treaty: royalties 0% for certain IP (e.g., copyright) or 10% for others; interest 0% if arm's length, otherwise 15%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 for goods transactions; CAD 500,000 for services; CAD 250,000 for intangibles (annual aggregate with non-residents).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada applies General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and requires economic substance for treaty benefits; no specific ESR regime, but transactions must have commercial rationale.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false deductions, or fraudulent misrepresentation in T2 return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Income Tax Act s.239; fines up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they failed to withhold or remit; civil penalties and potential travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporation without real business activity, used to artificially shift profits or avoid Canadian tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment; denial of treaty benefits; penalties up to 50% of tax avoided.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for tax debts if company is a sham; potential criminal charges for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to report large cash transactions (over CAD 10,000) or suspicious transactions to FINTRAC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 2,000,000 for corporations; criminal penalties for deliberate non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be fined up to CAD 500,000 and imprisoned up to 5 years for knowingly failing to comply.
